title: The Digital-Currency Divide
gist: Paywalled teaser: Howard Davies notes that the push for central bank digital currencies has slowed amid underwhelming demand and rising costs, with the Federal Reserve and other central banks shelving plans, while the ECB presses ahead with a digital euro.

themes.theme: CBDC retreat and the ECB's digital-euro holdout

insights.claim: The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts.
insights.speaker: Howard Davies
insights.so_what: CBDC momentum is fading globally, which shifts digital-money competition toward private stablecoins and payment rails.
insights.quote: underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts

insights.claim: The Federal Reserve and other central banks have shelved their CBDC plans, while the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro, creating a transatlantic digital-currency divide.
insights.speaker: Howard Davies
insights.so_what: Watch the digital-euro rollout as the main live CBDC project among major economies and its effect on European banks and payments.
insights.quote: the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro

insights.claim: Seven years earlier, Facebook's Libra project, headed by David Marcus, was pitched to bankers and central bankers at the Group of Thirty seminar as making banking cheaper and easier for the unbanked in emerging markets.
insights.speaker: Howard Davies
insights.so_what: Historical context: private-currency threats like Libra originally spurred central-bank digital-currency efforts.
